concepts.def: German school (1919-1933) merging art, craft and industry; clean geometric forms.
1920s-30s decorative style using geometric shapes, bold colours, luxurious materials.
Early-20th-century movement: 'form follows function'; minimal ornament.
Late-20th-century reaction; playful, eclectic, ironic; e.g., Ettore Sottsass and the Memphis group.
Braun designer (1932-); 'less but better'; 10 principles of good design.
British inventor; bagless vacuum (1983), iterative design ethos.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Design Influences — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Design Influences brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Design Influences.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
